summary.text: A 49-year-old man with atopic dermatitis, bronchial asthma, hypertension, cataracts and glaucoma, with multiple drug and food allergies, presented with persistent ear pruritus. Atopic dermatitis had been managed since childhood, and dupilumab fourteen months earlier markedly improved the trunk lesions, but severe ear pruritus persisted despite topical steroid ear drops and steroid ointments, prompting referral.

Initial otoscopic examination showed erythema and abundant scaling in the external auditory canal, with scales and erythema also on the tympanic membrane in the figure. Serum IgE and TARC had fallen after dupilumab but stayed above normal ranges, allergy testing showed high sensitization to multiple environmental and food antigens, and cultures grew only commensal bacteria with no pathogenic organisms.

Because symptoms persisted despite steroid therapy, the authors instructed the patient on application technique and started delgocitinib ointment 0.5% twice daily to the external ear. After one month he showed substantial improvement with resolution of scaling and reduced erythema, and the steroid ointment was discontinued, delgocitinib continuing alone.

He was then followed up every two months and remained stable, needing only one to two applications of delgocitinib per week. Remission was sustained after one year of intermittent use without corticosteroids, with normal otoscopic findings bilaterally in the figure, and the authors report greater improvement than with topical steroids.

ambiguities.issue: The article names the diagnosis both as chronic external otitis (abstract) and as external ear eczema (introduction and discussion) and never states that they are the same entity.

This report presents a case of external ear eczema

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not merge the two diagnoses into one or add infectious otitis externa; both are recorded as the source words them.

evidence.quote: steroid ointments (betamethasone valerate and gentamicin sulfate)
